analysis.title: The Brink's Co. (BCO): 3Q AMS/DRS momentum and earlier NATL close strengthen earnings outlook
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on BCO with a 12-month price target of $135 (from $134), 25.0% upside from the $108.00 price as of the 3 Nov 2026 close. The target uses an unchanged 6.75x EV/EBITDA on a rolled-forward NTM + 1YR EBITDA estimate of $1,168mn.

3Q26 results were mixed. Revenue of $1,375mn rose 3.0% y/y, below GS's 3.5% estimate and FactSet consensus of 3.8%. Organic revenue grew 3.6% y/y against GS's 5.1% forecast and 4.1% in 2Q. Adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted EPS beat, and the full-year guide was reaffirmed.

Digital Retail Solutions (DRS) and ATM Managed Services (AMS) combined grew 16%+ organically in 3Q, up from 14% in 2Q. This was the 15th consecutive quarter of at least mid-teens growth. BCO expects another sequential acceleration in 4Q despite lapping a large prior-year equipment sale.

North American DRS backlog rose 80% y/y and is broad-based across customers from tens of locations to several thousand. The previously announced 5,500-location retailer accounts for only part of the increase. Other growth drivers include the Luxembourg Bancomat rollout, Bank Mandiri, Mexico wins and a new Canadian bank contract.

DRS/AMS reached a record 32% of quarterly revenue. BCO converted $48mn of organic revenue growth into $24mn of incremental EBITDA, about 50% flow-through, and EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps y/y. North America reached 20% TTM EBITDA margins, up more than 500 bps since 2022. Europe margins rose more than 400 bps y/y.

Cash and Valuables Management (CVM) organic revenue fell 1.5% y/y. AMS/DRS conversions created roughly twice the 1-2% organic headwind of prior quarters, and Global Services volumes moderated toward historical levels after elevated precious metals transportation activity. BCO expects both pressures to continue in 4Q.

Some customers are delaying longer-term AMS and ATM-as-a-Service decisions by a couple of months until they can evaluate the combined BCO and NCR Atleos (NATL) offering. GS reads this as timing rather than lost demand.

BCO now expects the NATL acquisition to close in early January 2027, nearly a full quarter earlier than first contemplated. Foreign direct investment and money transmitter licensing conditions are satisfied, and antitrust reviews are resolved in 12 major jurisdictions. UK and EU reviews remain in progress.

Integration teams target the full $200mn run-rate cost synergy by the end of 2029, and have identified additional savings beyond that target in procurement, real estate, SG&A and service network optimization. BCO is still quantifying the upside and may give details with 4Q results in February.

BCO expects the combination to expand its addressable market to 2-3x the current $36bn global market. The 5,500-location retail win shows the potential to service DRS devices and Allpoint ATMs in a single trip.

The planned NoteMachine and TestLink UK divestitures, required for the NATL close, carry £120-130mn of revenue and about £30mn of EBITDA. Sale proceeds are uncertain because the buyer process is ongoing, and BCO did not say whether further regulatory remedies could be required. BCO says previously communicated deal returns remain intact.

FY26 guidance was reiterated: mid-single-digit organic revenue growth, EBITDA margin expansion of 30-50 bps (implied 18.9-19.1%) and free cash flow conversion of 40-45% of EBITDA. 4Q26 guidance is revenue of $1,365-$1,415mn, adjusted EBITDA of $275-295mn and EPS of $2.45-$2.80.

GS lowers 2026/2027/2028 revenue estimates to $5,532mn/$5,649mn/$5,946mn from $5,561mn/$5,725mn/$6,026mn, an average 1.1% cut, on a softer North America and Latin America outlook. EBITDA margin forecasts are unchanged at 19.0%/19.5%/20.1%. EPS estimates fall to $8.99/$10.06/$11.67 from $9.08/$10.25/$11.88.
The GS target multiple of 6.75x EV/EBITDA is at a discount to the Business Services peer group median of 8.7x, reflecting BCO's lower EBITDA margins and higher financial leverage.

market_movers.rationale: DRS/AMS mix shift, operating leverage and earlier NATL synergy capture support margin expansion and free cash flow improvement, offsetting near-term legacy revenue pressure. Price target raised from $134 to $135.

earnings_insights: BCO 3Q26 (reported 4 Nov 2026): revenue $1,374.6mn, +3.0% y/y reported and +3.6% organic, versus GS estimate +3.5% y/y and FactSet consensus +3.8% y/y.
BCO 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA margin 19.9% (+90 bps y/y), versus GS estimate 19.6% and consensus 19.6%. Adjusted EBITDA $273.6mn versus GS estimate $270.7mn.

BCO 3Q26 adjusted EPS $2.46 (non-GAAP, reported), versus GS estimate $2.40 and FactSet consensus $2.21. GAAP EPS was $0.35 versus GS estimate $2.04, on $87.0mn of one-time items including $65.2mn of other items not allocated to segments.

3Q26 segment revenue versus GS estimates: North America $439.9mn vs $460.3mn, Latin America $354.4mn vs $362.0mn, Europe $380.3mn vs $357.9mn, Rest of World $200.0mn vs $202.1mn. Organic growth by region: North America +1%, Latin America +2%, Europe +2%, Rest of World +14%. FX was a 1% headwind to revenue growth.

BCO 4Q26 company guidance: revenue $1,365-$1,415mn, organic growth 3.0-4.5%, reported growth (1)-3%, EBITDA $275-295mn (20.5% margin at midpoint), EPS $2.45-$2.80. GS prior 4Q26 estimates were revenue $1,411mn, EBITDA $290mn, EPS $2.75, versus FactSet consensus (pre-print) of $1,410mn, $287mn and $2.55.
GS new 4Q26 estimates: revenue $1,390.0mn, adjusted EBITDA $284.4mn (20.5% margin), adjusted EPS $2.59.

GS FY26E adjusted EPS cut to $8.99 from $9.08, against pre-print FactSet consensus of $9.02. GS FY26E revenue is $5,532mn (previously $5,561mn, pre-print consensus $5,563mn) and EBITDA $1,053mn on a 19.0% margin (pre-print consensus $1,053mn, 18.9%).

BCO expects FY26 organic revenue growth of mid-single digits, including mid-to-high teens DRS/AMS organic growth. GS says guidance points to stable consensus estimates for 2026 revenue and EBITDA margins.
risk_factors: Rising adoption of competing payment technologies and declines in cash usage.
Acquisition integration risk tied to NATL.
Regulatory remedies and UK/EU antitrust reviews: BCO did not say whether more remedies could be required beyond the planned UK divestitures, and sale proceeds remain uncertain.
Customer decision delays on AMS and ATM-as-a-Service awards while customers evaluate the combined BCO-NATL offering.
